svg.title: Bot of Culture review browser — early mockup
svg.desc: Mock server library on desktop and a global review profile on mobile. All people, titles, reviews and dates are fictional sample content. Library groups reviews by title, with a subtle Reviewed in another server text label only on an outside-origin review. An older game review edited on September 9 remains below a movie created September 8; edit dates never reorder reviews or title groups. Title search is confirmed for launch and searches stored title names. Search stays on the same screen and more results load automatically while scrolling. Neutral dark surfaces and a restrained blurple accent feel familiar in Discord’s browser without using Discord branding. Individual reviews use whole stars on the existing 1–5 scale. Server title summaries average the sample reviews: movie 3.5 stars from two reviews, game 5 stars from one. Profiles show only individual ratings. Visibility is managed through Discord. Category filters use one compact strip with a blurple underline on All; screens use server and profile headings without the internal bot name.
svg.text: Early design • all names, titles, reviews and dates are mock data
The ending stayed with me. Beautifully restrained.
A slow start, but the final act earns it.
One more run turned into forty hours.
Your reviews are public by default. Hide yours with /reviews visibility hidden in Discord.
Your reviews are public by default.
Title groups → member reviews → global profile. 1–5 stars. No web editor or login.
Edits keep their original position. Unknown edit history stays unmarked. Origin labels never reveal the source server.
